title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This Review discusses universal lower bounds on entropy production inferred from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Entropy production is a key measure of non-equilibrium behavior but is difficult to measure directly in partially observed systems; model-free bounds from coarse-grained observables are needed.
method: The Review surveys stochastic thermodynamics approaches that derive lower bounds on entropy production using fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories, including states, currents, correlations, and waiting times.
result: Universal bounds on entropy production are obtained from coarse-grained observables without detailed knowledge of the underlying dynamics, applicable to both steady and time-dependent regimes.
conclusion: These bounds provide practical tools for estimating dissipation in complex systems and highlight progress in trajectory-level estimation of entropy production.

title: Asynchronous Multi-photon Interference For Quantum Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates asynchronous multi-photon interference for quantum networks, enabling entanglement distribution without synchronization.
motivation: Synchronization of independent photon sources is a major challenge for scalable quantum networks; asynchronous interference relaxes this requirement.
method: The authors experimentally realize multi-photon interference from independent sources using a time-resolved detection scheme and post-selection.
result: They achieve high-visibility interference and entanglement swapping without active synchronization, demonstrating a key building block for quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Asynchronous multi-photon interference is a viable approach for practical quantum networks, reducing complexity and improving scalability.

title: A Hybrid Anyon-otto Thermal Machine
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum thermal machine using anyons in a fractional quantum Hall system, operating on an Otto cycle with non-Abelian anyonic working medium.
motivation: To explore the thermodynamic performance of topological systems and anyonic statistics in quantum thermal machines, bridging quantum thermodynamics and topological matter.
method: The authors model an Otto cycle where the working medium is a pair of anyons in a fractional quantum Hall system, with the cycle strokes involving changes in magnetic field and coupling to thermal baths. They compute work output and efficiency using anyonic braiding statistics.
result: The anyonic Otto engine can achieve high efficiency, with performance influenced by anyon statistics and topological degeneracy, and can operate in both engine and refrigerator modes.
conclusion: Anyonic systems offer a new platform for quantum thermal machines, with potential advantages from topological protection and non-Abelian statistics.

title: A Unified Optical Platform For non-Gaussian And Fault-tolerant Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill States
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified optical platform for generating non-Gaussian and fault-tolerant Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, advancing quantum error correction and optical quantum computing.
motivation: GKP states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but are challenging to generate experimentally. A unified platform that can produce both non-Gaussian and fault-tolerant GKP states is needed to enable scalable optical quantum computing.
method: The authors use a combination of squeezed light sources, beam splitters, and photon-number-resolving detectors to implement a measurement-based protocol for GKP state generation. They optimize the experimental setup to achieve high-fidelity states.
result: They successfully generate GKP states with high squeezing levels and demonstrate fault-tolerant error correction capabilities. The platform is versatile and can produce a variety of non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The unified optical platform provides a practical path toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with GKP states, bridging the gap between theory and experiment in optical quantum information processing.

title: Photonic Qubit Gates Via 1d Scattering From An Array Of Two-level Emitters
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a photonic quantum gate using 1D scattering from an array of two-level emitters.
motivation: To realize high-fidelity quantum gates for photonic qubits, which are essential for quantum networks and computing.
method: Analyzes scattering of single photons from a chain of two-level emitters coupled to a waveguide, deriving effective gate operations via controlled-phase shifts.
result: Demonstrates that the array can implement controlled-phase and other two-qubit gates with high fidelity and low loss.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a scalable and integrable platform for photonic quantum information processing.

title: Advantage Of Quantum Machine Learning From General Computational Advantages
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper establishes a general framework linking computational advantages in quantum machine learning to broader quantum computational advantages, providing rigorous theoretical foundations.
motivation: Quantum machine learning promises speedups, but the precise conditions under which such advantages arise are not fully understood. The authors aim to clarify the relationship between quantum machine learning advantages and general quantum computational advantages.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that connects the performance of quantum machine learning algorithms to underlying quantum computational primitives, using concepts from computational complexity and information theory.
result: They prove that any quantum machine learning advantage can be traced back to a general quantum computational advantage, and characterize the types of problems where such advantages are possible.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on quantum machine learning advantages, showing they are not isolated but stem from fundamental quantum computational capabilities, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Thermodynamic Sampling Of Materials Using Neutral-atom Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a thermodynamic sampling method using neutral-atom quantum computers to efficiently explore the potential energy landscape of materials.
motivation: Traditional computational methods for materials discovery are limited by the exponential complexity of exploring high-dimensional potential energy surfaces. Quantum computers may offer a speedup for sampling low-energy configurations.
method: The authors map the problem of sampling materials configurations to the ground state preparation of a quantum Hamiltonian, using neutral-atom quantum computers with Rydberg interactions to perform quantum annealing or variational quantum algorithms.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum approach can find lower-energy configurations more efficiently than classical simulated annealing for certain small material systems, and discuss scaling to larger systems.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers show promise for thermodynamic sampling in materials science, but further hardware improvements and algorithmic refinements are needed for practical advantage.

title: Artificial Intelligence For Representing And Characterizing Quantum Systems
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 29 July 2026;
tldr: This Technical Review surveys how AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, and language models, are used to represent and characterize complex quantum systems.
motivation: The intersection of AI and quantum information science is rapidly growing, and a comprehensive overview is needed to map the field and identify key methods and applications.
method: The review categorizes AI approaches for quantum state representation, quantum process tomography, and Hamiltonian learning, discussing both classical and quantum machine learning models.
result: It highlights that AI methods, especially neural networks and kernel methods, can efficiently represent high-dimensional quantum states and processes, and that language models are emerging as tools for quantum system characterization.
conclusion: AI provides powerful new tools for quantum information science, enabling the study of systems that are otherwise intractable, and this cross-disciplinary field is expected to expand further.

title: The Role Of Data-induced Randomness In Quantum Machine Learning Classification Tasks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates how data-induced randomness affects classification tasks in quantum machine learning.
motivation: Understanding the role of randomness in quantum machine learning is important for designing robust classifiers, but the paper's focus is on practical performance rather than fundamental information-theoretic limits.
method: The authors analyze classification tasks using quantum models and study the impact of randomness inherent in the data, likely through numerical simulations or theoretical analysis of error bounds.
result: The paper characterizes how data-induced randomness influences classification accuracy and provides insights into the trade-offs involved.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of quantum machine learning but are more applied and incremental, not directly advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Mixed-state Order In A Hubbard Quantum Simulator
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports an experimental observation of a topological phase transition in a Hubbard quantum simulator using ultracold erbium atoms, and shows that the transition disappears when two systems are stacked or disorder information is lost.
motivation: Topological phases are hard to distinguish with local measurements; the authors aim to reveal a transition between such phases and study the effect of stacking and disorder.
method: They use a quantum simulator based on ultracold erbium atoms in an optical lattice to realize a Hubbard model, and measure topological order via local observables.
result: A topological phase transition is observed, and it vanishes when two copies are stacked or when information about disorder is lost, indicating mixed-state order.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new way to detect topological phase transitions in quantum simulators and highlights the fragility of topological order under decoherence.

title: Reply To: Conductance Measurements Cannot Distinguish Crossed Andreev Reflection From Elastic Co-tunnelling In Normal–superconductor–normal Junctions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that conductance measurements cannot distinguish crossed Andreev reflection from elastic co-tunnelling in normal-superconductor-normal junctions.
motivation: The authors respond to a claim that conductance measurements can distinguish these two processes, which is important for understanding transport in superconducting hybrid structures.
method: The paper provides a theoretical analysis showing that both processes produce identical conductance signatures, making them indistinguishable via conductance alone.
result: Conductance measurements are insufficient to differentiate crossed Andreev reflection from elastic co-tunnelling.
conclusion: Alternative measurement techniques are needed to distinguish these two transport mechanisms.

title: Superconductivity With A Squeeze
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of superconductivity under pressure in the van der Waals metal CeSiI, providing a new platform for studying dimensionality and Kondo physics.
motivation: To explore superconductivity in a layered van der Waals material under pressure, which may reveal new physics related to dimensionality and Kondo interactions.
method: The authors applied pressure to CeSiI and measured its superconducting properties.
result: Superconductivity was observed under pressure in CeSiI.
conclusion: CeSiI offers a new platform for studying the interplay of dimensionality and Kondo physics in superconductivity.

title: Conductance Measurements Cannot Distinguish Crossed Andreev Reflection From Elastic Co-tunnelling In Normal–superconductor–normal Junctions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: The paper shows that conductance measurements cannot distinguish crossed Andreev reflection from elastic co-tunnelling in normal-superconductor-normal junctions.
motivation: Distinguishing crossed Andreev reflection from elastic co-tunnelling is important for understanding transport in superconductor-normal junctions, but the paper argues it is impossible via conductance alone.
method: The authors analyze the conductance of normal-superconductor-normal junctions theoretically and compare the signatures of crossed Andreev reflection and elastic co-tunnelling.
result: They find that both processes produce identical conductance contributions, making them indistinguishable in conductance measurements.
conclusion: Alternative measurement techniques beyond conductance are needed to differentiate these two transport mechanisms.

title: Superconductivity Under Pressure In A Van Der Waals Heavy-fermion Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of superconductivity under pressure in a van der Waals heavy-fermion metal, focusing on the interplay between antiferromagnetism, Kondo coherence, and unconventional superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the pressure-induced superconductivity and its relationship with magnetic order and Kondo physics in a two-dimensional heavy-fermion system.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to the material and measure electrical transport and magnetic properties to map the phase diagram.
result: They observe a dome-shaped superconducting phase that emerges near the suppression of antiferromagnetic order, indicating a quantum critical point.
conclusion: The study reveals a rich phase diagram in a van der Waals heavy-fermion metal, highlighting the role of dimensionality in unconventional superconductivity.

title: Real-time Optical Signal Equalization With A Silicon Photonic Spatially Distributed Reservoir Computer
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates real-time optical signal equalization using a silicon photonic reservoir computer.
motivation: To mitigate fiber distortions in high-speed optical communication without digital signal processing.
method: A spatially distributed reservoir computer implemented on a silicon photonic chip processes a 28-Gbps on-off keying signal in real time.
result: Bit error rates as low as 4 × 10^-7 are achieved.
conclusion: Photonic reservoir computing is a viable approach for real-time equalization in optical communication.

title: Emergence Of Fermi-liquid And Bcs Physics In Overdoped Cuprates
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that observed behaviors in overdoped cuprates can be explained by substitutional disorder in a d-wave superconductor, rather than requiring non-Fermi-liquid physics.
motivation: To resolve the apparent inconsistency between weak-coupling Fermi-liquid theory and experimental observations in overdoped cuprates.
method: The authors present a perspective based on theoretical arguments and analysis of substitutional disorder effects in d-wave superconductors.
result: They propose that in the disorder-free limit, a weak-coupling Fermi-liquid-based BCS description is possible.
conclusion: Substitutional disorder is key to understanding overdoped cuprate behavior, and disorder-free systems may align with conventional theory.

title: Experimental Implementation Of A Discrete-time Quantum Walk On Biological Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 July 2026;
tldr: This paper experimentally implements a discrete-time quantum walk on biological networks, demonstrating quantum dynamics on graph structures derived from biological data.
motivation: To explore quantum information processing on complex biological network topologies, potentially for modeling biological processes or quantum simulation.
method: A discrete-time quantum walk is implemented on a photonic platform, with the walker's evolution governed by coin operators and shift operators defined on biological network graphs.
result: The experimental implementation successfully shows quantum interference and probability distributions characteristic of quantum walks on non-regular graphs.
conclusion: Quantum walks can be realized on biological network structures, opening avenues for quantum simulation of biological systems but not directly advancing core quantum information theory or hardware.

title: Phonon Focusing At Room Temperature
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates phonon focusing at room temperature, enabling directional heat control via crystal orientation.
motivation: Phonon focusing, where heat flow is channeled along specific crystal directions, was previously only observed at low temperatures; achieving it at room temperature could enable new thermal management technologies.
method: The authors use experimental measurements and theoretical modeling to show that long-lived phonon waves persist at room temperature and that heat transport depends on crystal orientation.
result: They observe clear phonon focusing effects at room temperature, with heat flow strongly anisotropic and following crystallographic directions.
conclusion: Room-temperature phonon focusing offers opportunities for directional heat control in future technologies, such as thermal management in electronics.

title: Manipulating Spin Dynamics Via Exciton–exciton Interactions For Bright Spin Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates spin light-emitting diodes with high dissymmetry factor and long lifetime by manipulating exciton–exciton interactions in hybrid chiral metal halide heterostructures.
motivation: To achieve bright spin light-emitting diodes that directly emit circularly polarized light, which is important for spintronics and optoelectronics.
method: The authors use exciton–exciton interactions in hybrid chiral metal halide heterostructures to suppress spin relaxation.
result: They achieve a dissymmetry factor of 0.2 and a half-lifetime of 5,000 hours at an initial luminance of 100 cd m−2.
conclusion: Manipulating exciton–exciton interactions is an effective strategy for improving the performance of spin light-emitting diodes.

title: Universities Need Transparent Quantum Hardware
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that universities should procure transparent quantum hardware for educational purposes rather than relying solely on cloud access.
motivation: The authors believe that students need hands-on experience with quantum hardware to understand the gap between ideal circuits and physical measurements.
method: The paper presents a perspective based on educational needs and the limitations of cloud-based quantum computing access.
result: It concludes that universities should invest in teachable quantum systems that allow students to see and interact with the hardware.
conclusion: Transparent quantum hardware is essential for effective quantum education at the university level.

title: Standards In Space
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 July 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the need for gold-standard references in space to monitor long-term Earth system trends from satellite instruments.

result: No new results; the paper is a commentary on the importance of calibration standards.

title: Dynamics Of Supracellular Keratin Bundling And Nuclear Uncaging In Stretched Epithelia
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical response of epithelial cells under large deformation, focusing on keratin filament bundling and nuclear uncaging.
motivation: Understanding how cells protect the nucleus from mechanical stress is important for cell biology and tissue mechanics.
method: The authors apply large deformations to epithelial tissues and observe the dynamics of supracellular keratin bundles and nuclear uncaging using microscopy.
result: Under large deformations, intermediate filaments bundle and ultimately release the nucleus from its cage.
conclusion: The study reveals a mechanism for nuclear protection under extreme mechanical stress.

title: Large-scale Compressive Microscopy Via Diffractive Multiplexing Across A Sensor Array
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a high-speed, large-area computational microscope using diffractive multiplexing and compressive sensing across a sensor array.
motivation: To achieve gigapixel-per-second imaging with micrometer resolution over centimeter-scale fields of view, which is challenging with conventional microscopy.
method: An array of 48 sensors combined with a diffractive mask and compressive sensing algorithms to multiplex and reconstruct high-resolution images.
result: Demonstrated 25 gigapixel-per-second imaging at 120 frames per second with micrometer resolution across multi-centimeter areas.
conclusion: The approach enables high-throughput, large-area microscopy suitable for applications like biomedical imaging and materials science.

title: Enhanced Inverse Compton Scattering Via Spontaneous Focusing Induced By A Coated Plasma Mirror
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced inverse Compton scattering efficiency using a coated plasma mirror to focus laser pulses, achieving 10^-3 efficiency and photon energies up to hundreds of MeV.
motivation: Inverse Compton scattering is a key mechanism for generating high-energy photons, but its efficiency is typically low. Enhancing efficiency could enable compact, high-brightness gamma-ray sources.
method: A coated plasma mirror is used to spontaneously focus the reflected laser pulse, increasing the intensity at the interaction point with a relativistic electron beam.
result: The efficiency reaches 10^-3 with photon energies extending to hundreds of megaelectronvolts at a laser power of 400 TW.
conclusion: The coated plasma mirror approach significantly improves inverse Compton scattering efficiency, offering a path to practical high-energy photon sources.
